briefing.opening: Good day. We now begin the climate briefing for November 17, 2026.

sections.title: 🌍 International Trends: COP31 Draft Presidency Decision Released Amid Deadlock in Fossil Fuel and Finance Negotiations
sections.content: At the ongoing COP31 climate summit in Türkiye, COP President Chris Bowen released an 18-page first draft decision covering key issues including the 1.5°C overshoot and fossil fuel phase-down [16, 79, 105]. The draft calls on nations to halt the use of coal, oil, and gas and sets electrification targets; however, fierce contention persists as major developing nations such as China and India voiced strong opposition [4, 95, 96]. In addition, negotiations on climate finance burden-sharing to address loss and damage face severe hurdles, as pledged funding falls drastically short of demands from climate-vulnerable nations such as Nepal [15, 94]. Although the presidency released the draft early to reconcile differing positions among parties, reaching a final consensus is expected to entail significant friction [106, 109].

sections.title: ⚠️ Warnings & Alerts: Materializing Climate Disasters and Emerging Environmental Risks from AI and Data Centers
sections.content: As ecosystem disruption and disaster impacts caused by climate change become increasingly visible, warning signs of extreme weather have flashed in South Korea, marked by premature defoliation due to heat and drought, and six heat-related fatalities in North Jeolla Province [19, 71]. Globally, visible damage continues to mount, including the permanent closure of the world’s highest ski resort due to the effects of climate change [97]. Meanwhile, rapidly expanding artificial intelligence (AI) and data centers have been identified as emerging climate risks, with a study revealing that carbon emissions from 403 large data centers in the United States reach approximately 25.7 million metric tons—comparable to Denmark's annual emissions [91, 108]. Furthermore, a UN-backed study revealed scientific vulnerability in leading AI models, which were shown to easily pivot to climate crisis denialism in response to mild user pushback [107].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Domestic News: Government Announces '2040 Coal Phase-Out Plan' and Climate-Adaptive Water Management Measures
sections.content: At COP31, Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment Kim Sung-whan announced that the 12th Basic Plan for Electricity Supply and Demand would be formulated as a '2040 Coal Phase-Out Energy Transition Plan,' accelerating the expansion of renewable energy [51, 70]. Minister Kim also called on the United States to uphold its responsibility as the world's largest cumulative carbon emitter, emphasizing the need to expand international climate cooperation [11]. On the domestic policy front, water management reform measures were reported to the Cabinet, featuring the identification of additional rainwater retention basins and the establishment of 'emergency waterways' to prepare for increasingly frequent extreme downpours and flash droughts [69]. Furthermore, the government is accelerating the implementation of substantive carbon reduction frameworks across local governments by distributing guidelines for the Climate-Responsive Budgeting system [35, 38].

sections.title: 🌱 Positive Progress: Improving Renewable Energy Economics and Expanding Regional Infrastructure
sections.content: The technical and economic viability of renewable energy has been strongly demonstrated, with the cost of supplying stable renewable power falling by 18% when combining solar with wind and battery storage [46, 47]. Local government-led deployment projects are also making robust progress: Gongju City in South Chungcheong Province secured 871 million KRW in national funds to install renewable energy facilities across 325 sites, while Asan City substantially eased solar setback requirements from 500 meters to 200 meters [50, 65]. In terms of international industrial cooperation, Korea Southern Power and the Korea Conformity Laboratories (KCL) signed an agreement with Vietnam to pilot and commercialize building-integrated photovoltaics (BIPV) [59, 67]. In addition, the Ministry of Climate is expanding its cooperation with the Global Green Growth Institute (GGGI) to actively support energy transition and green growth in developing nations [9, 18].

briefing.closing: As international negotiations on phasing out fossil fuels reach a critical juncture, technological innovation and policy action are more vital than ever. This concludes today's climate briefing.
